model.rationale: The district's 21-point Democratic lean, Jasmine Clark's overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending advantage over Jonathan Chavez, and market pricing near 96 percent keep this open seat safely Democratic despite the absence of polls or expert ratings.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or significant outside spending against Clark would be the main signal to revisit this rating.

Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 13th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward Democrats. Incumbent Everton Blair is not on the ballot after losing the nomination for the full term, leaving Democrat Jasmine Clark and Republican Jonathan Chavez to compete for the open seat. Clark enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised roughly $2.4 million and drawn more than $4.2 million in outside support, while Chavez shows no reported fundraising. No outside groups have spent against Clark.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, campaign finance, and prediction markets, which price Clark's chances around 96 percent. The combination of a heavily Democratic electorate and a lopsided money advantage makes this seat safe for Democrats, with the open-seat dynamic the main source of residual uncertainty.
